issues.legal_issue: The sale deed was duly executed by the vendor and presented for registration.
The sale consideration was paid for the sale deed.
Registration of a sale deed after a lengthy delay does not invalidate it when it was duly presented for registration and the deficiency in stamp duty was later paid.
A registered sale deed is presumed correct unless its validity is successfully challenged.
Failure to mutate the purchasers’ names in revenue records does not extinguish rights created by a valid sale deed.
A vendor who has executed a sale deed and transferred the property cannot retain title merely because registration remained pending for a deficiency in stamp duty.
A sale deed in favour of purchasers who were minors is not void where a natural guardian acted on their behalf.
A subsequent purchaser cannot claim bona fide purchaser protection when the vendor had already transferred the property and no longer had title to convey.
A purchaser’s signature on a sale deed was not mandatory under the law applicable when the deed was presented for registration.
The subsequent sale deed is liable to be cancelled where the vendor had already transferred the property under an earlier valid sale deed.
